content:
Overview

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) is a central sector scheme that provides free assisted living devices to senior citizens belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category. Launched in 2017, the scheme distributes aids such as walking sticks, hearing aids, wheelchairs, and spectacles to elderly persons aged 60 years and above. The devices are provided through camps organised by the implementing agency, the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO).

Eligibility Criteria

  • Senior citizens aged 60 years and above
  • Belonging to Below Poverty Line families
  • Identification through the Socio Economic Caste Census (SECC) database
  • Persons with low vision, hearing impairment, or locomotor disability are the focus

Benefits

  • Free assisted living devices such as walkers, wheelchairs, hearing aids, and spectacles
  • Devices are customised to the beneficiary's requirements
  • Distribution through camps at block and district level
  • Improved mobility, hearing, and vision for elderly persons

How to Apply

  1. Eligible senior citizens are identified through the SECC database
  2. Attend the distribution camp organised in your area when notified
  3. Complete the assessment and receive the device at the camp

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card
  • BPL identification from the SECC list
  • Age proof
meta_title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana: Free Aids for Senior Citizens
meta_description: RVY provides free assisted living devices like wheelchairs and hearing aids to BPL senior citizens aged 60+. Check eligibility and distribution process.

content:
Overview

The National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities is a statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The National Trust works for the care, protection, and empowerment of persons with these disabilities, with a special focus on enabling them to live independently. It implements schemes such as Nirmaya health insurance, care giver training, and supported living arrangements.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Persons with autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, or multiple disabilities
  • Families and caregivers of such persons can also avail support services
  • Registration with the National Trust is required for many schemes

Benefits

  • Nirmaya health insurance cover for treatment and therapy of registered persons
  • Care giver training and respite care support
  • Supported employment and supported living arrangements
  • Legal guardianship support for families of persons with disabilities

How to Apply

  1. Register the person with a disability on the National Trust portal
  2. Apply for the specific scheme such as Nirmaya health insurance online
  3. Submit the disability certificate and family details for approval

Required Documents

  • Disability certificate from a recognised medical authority
  • Aadhaar card of the person and family
  • Bank account details
meta_title: National Trust: Support for Autism, CP & Intellectual Disability
meta_description: The National Trust provides health insurance, caregiver training, and supported living for persons with autism, cerebral palsy, and intellectual disabilities.

content:
Overview

The Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS) provides financial assistance to non-governmental organisations working for the education, training, and rehabilitation of persons with disabilities. Under the scheme, NGOs receive grants for running special schools, vocational training centres, and rehabilitation services for persons with visual, hearing, speech, locomotor, and intellectual disabilities. The scheme aims to make persons with disabilities self reliant and productive.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Registered non-governmental organisations working for persons with disabilities
  • NGOs must have experience and capacity to run rehabilitation programmes
  • Beneficiaries are persons with disabilities receiving education, training, or rehabilitation services

Benefits

  • Grants for special schools and vocational training centres
  • Support for rehabilitation services and aids distribution
  • Skill development and livelihood training for persons with disabilities
  • Community based rehabilitation programme support

How to Apply

  1. NGOs apply online through the Disability Common Application portal
  2. Submit the project proposal and registration documents
  3. Approved organisations receive grants for the sanctioned activities

Required Documents

  • NGO registration certificate and experience details
  • Project proposal with budget
  • Annual reports and audited statements
meta_title: Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme: NGO Grants
meta_description: DDRS funds NGOs running special schools and rehabilitation centres for persons with disabilities. Check grant eligibility and application process.

content:
Overview

The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is a statutory body established under the Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005. The commission works to protect and promote the rights of children in India, including the right to education, protection from exploitation, and access to health and nutrition. It examines laws, policies, and complaints related to child rights violations and recommends corrective action to governments.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any citizen can file a complaint regarding violation of child rights with the commission
  • Children, parents, and civil society organisations can approach the commission
  • The commission also takes suo motu cognisance of reported violations

Benefits

  • Complaint redressal mechanism for child rights violations
  • Inquiry into cases of child labour, trafficking, abuse, and denial of education
  • Recommendations to state and central governments for policy changes
  • Awareness programmes on child rights and protection laws

How to Apply

  1. File a complaint through the NCPCR e-Baal Nidan portal or by post
  2. Provide details of the violation and the affected child
  3. The commission inquires into the matter and follows up with the concerned authorities

Required Documents

  • Details of the complaint with supporting evidence
  • Identity and contact details of the complainant
meta_title: NCPCR: Child Rights Protection & Complaint Redressal
meta_description: NCPCR protects child rights in India, handling complaints on child labour, abuse, and denial of education. Learn how to file a complaint.

content:
Overview

The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 is a comprehensive law enacted to protect children from sexual abuse, harassment, and exploitation. The Act defines offences against children and prescribes stringent punishments, with a special focus on speedy trial and child friendly procedures. It also establishes the framework for reporting, recording, and investigating such offences, with the Special Court and Child Welfare Committee playing key roles.

Eligibility Criteria

  • The Act applies to all children below 18 years of age in India
  • Any person aware of a sexual offence against a child is legally bound to report it
  • Protection applies irrespective of gender of the child

Benefits

  • Stringent legal punishment for sexual offences against children
  • Child friendly procedures during investigation and trial
  • Mandatory reporting requirement for every citizen
  • Support and protection for child victims through the child protection system

How to Apply

  1. Report the offence to the nearest police station or the Childline helpline 1098
  2. The police register an FIR and follow the procedures laid down in the Act
  3. The child receives support through the Child Welfare Committee and counselling services

Required Documents

  • No documents are required to report an offence; the FIR is registered based on the complaint
meta_title: POCSO Act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences
meta_description: POCSO Act 2012 protects children below 18 from sexual abuse with stringent punishment and child friendly procedures. Know how to report.

content:
Overview

The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 is the primary law for children in need of care and protection and children in conflict with the law in India. The Act provides a child friendly approach to justice, establishing Juvenile Justice Boards and Child Welfare Committees across districts. It also governs adoption, foster care, and rehabilitation of children through institutions and after care programmes.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Children in need of care and protection, including orphans, abandoned, and abused children
  • Children in conflict with the law, below 18 years of age
  • Families seeking adoption of children can approach the designated authorities

Benefits

  • Rehabilitation and reintegration of children through Child Welfare Committees
  • Child friendly procedures for children in conflict with the law
  • Legal framework for adoption and foster care
  • Protection from abuse in institutional care settings

How to Apply

  1. Children in need of care can be brought to the Child Welfare Committee through Childline 1098 or the police
  2. Adoption applications are filed through the Central Adoption Resource Authority portal
  3. Rehabilitation services follow the orders of the concerned committee or board

Required Documents

  • As specified by the Child Welfare Committee or the adoption authority
meta_title: Juvenile Justice Act: Care, Protection & Adoption of Children
meta_description: The Juvenile Justice Act 2015 governs care, protection, adoption, and rehabilitation of children in India. Understand its provisions and process.

content:
Overview

The National Programme for the Healthcare of the Elderly (NPHCE) component focuses on preventive, promotive, and curative healthcare for senior citizens in India. Under this programme, geriatric departments and outpatient clinics are established at district hospitals, along with regional geriatric centres at medical colleges. The programme trains healthcare personnel in geriatric care and provides community based services for the elderly.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all persons aged 60 years and above
  • Services are available at government health facilities with geriatric departments
  • No income or category restrictions apply

Benefits

  • Geriatric OPDs for consultation and treatment at district hospitals
  • Care for age related conditions such as arthritis, diabetes, hypertension, and dementia
  • Rehabilitation and physiotherapy at regional geriatric centres
  • Health education and awareness for elderly persons and caregivers

How to Apply

  1. Visit the geriatric department of a government hospital
  2. Register as a patient and undergo the medical assessment
  3. Attend follow-ups and rehabilitation sessions as advised

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card or any government-issued identity proof
  • Previous medical records, if any
meta_title: National Programme for Aged: Geriatric Care at Govt Hospitals
meta_description: The National Programme for the Healthcare of the Elderly provides geriatric OPDs, treatment, and rehabilitation for senior citizens. Check eligibility.

content:
Overview

Childline 1098 is India's 24-hour free emergency helpline for children in need of care and protection. Operated by the Ministry of Women and Child Development through partner organisations, Childline responds to calls from children facing abuse, exploitation, homelessness, or any form of distress. The service connects children to rescue, medical, and rehabilitation support through its network across the country.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any child in distress can call 1098 free of charge
  • Adults aware of a child in distress can also call on behalf of the child
  • The service is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

Benefits

  • Immediate response to calls from children in distress
  • Rescue and medical assistance through partner organisations
  • Rehabilitation support and shelter for children in need
  • Confidential and child friendly handling of every call

How to Apply

  1. Dial 1098 from any phone, free of cost
  2. Explain the situation to the counsellor
  3. Childline teams respond and provide the necessary support

Required Documents

  • No documents are required to call the helpline
meta_title: Childline 1098: 24-Hour Helpline for Children in Distress
meta_description: Childline 1098 is a free 24-hour emergency helpline for children in distress in India. Learn when to call and how the service helps children.

content:
Overview

Ujjawala is a comprehensive scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development for the prevention of trafficking and rescue, rehabilitation, and reintegration of victims of trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation. The scheme provides shelter, food, clothing, medical care, and counselling to rescued victims through protective and rehabilitative homes. It also supports awareness campaigns and community based prevention efforts.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Women and children rescued from trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation
  • Women and children vulnerable to trafficking can access prevention services
  • Rehabilitation support is provided through implementing NGOs and state agencies

Benefits

  • Safe shelter, food, clothing, and medical care for rescued victims
  • Psychological counselling and legal aid support
  • Skill training and livelihood support for reintegration
  • Educational support for children rescued from trafficking

How to Apply

  1. Rescued victims are brought to the protective home through the police or child protection system
  2. NGOs implementing the scheme provide intake and rehabilitation services
  3. Beneficiaries receive support as per the individual rehabilitation plan

Required Documents

  • Identity details as available; documentation is facilitated by the rehabilitation centre
meta_title: Ujjawala Scheme: Anti-Trafficking Rescue & Rehabilitation
meta_description: Ujjawala scheme prevents trafficking and provides shelter, medical care, counselling, and skill training for rescued victims. Learn how it works.

content:
Overview

The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development that safeguards the rights of children in India. It reviews existing laws and policies affecting children, examines complaints of rights violations, and recommends corrective measures to governments. The commission covers all children up to 18 years of age across education, health, protection, and participation rights.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any citizen, child, or organisation can bring child rights violations to the commission's notice
  • Complaints can relate to any child below 18 years of age
  • The commission can also act on its own initiative on reported matters

Benefits

  • Redressal of complaints related to child rights violations
  • Inquiries into child labour, abuse, trafficking, and denial of education and health care
  • Policy recommendations and monitoring of child rights implementation
  • Public awareness and advocacy on child rights issues

How to Apply

  1. File a complaint on the e-Baal Nidan portal or send a written complaint
  2. Provide complete details and evidence of the violation
  3. Track the inquiry and follow-up through the portal

Required Documents

  • Complaint details with supporting evidence
  • Contact details of the complainant
meta_title: NCPCR: File Child Rights Complaint Online (e-Baal Nidan)
meta_description: NCPCR protects children's rights in India, examining complaints of violations and recommending policy action. Learn how to file a complaint.

content:
Overview

Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is a small savings scheme of the Government of India for the welfare of the girl child. Under the scheme, a savings account is opened in the name of a girl child below 10 years of age, and deposits earn a high interest rate with income tax benefits. The accumulated amount supports the girl's education and marriage expenses, making it one of the most popular investment options for parents of daughters.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Account can be opened for a girl child below 10 years of age
  • Only one account per girl child; a maximum of two accounts per family (with exceptions for twins)
  • Deposits can be made by parents or legal guardians

Benefits

  • Attractive interest rate, revised periodically by the government
  • Income tax deduction on deposits and tax free interest and maturity amount
  • Partial withdrawal allowed for the girl's education after she turns 18
  • Account matures after 21 years from the date of opening, or on marriage after 18 years

How to Apply

  1. Visit any post office or authorised commercial bank branch
  2. Fill the SSY account opening form with the girl child's details
  3. Deposit the minimum initial amount and submit the required documents
  4. Deposits can be made in multiple instalments during the year

Required Documents

  • Birth certificate of the girl child
  • Aadhaar card of the child and the guardian
  • Identity and address proof of the guardian
meta_title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana: High Interest Savings for Girl Child
meta_description: SSY offers attractive interest, tax benefits, and long term savings for a girl child below 10 years. Check eligibility, deposits, and how to open.

content:
Overview

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) is a maternity benefit programme for pregnant women and lactating mothers in India. The scheme provides a cash benefit of Rs 5,000 in instalments for the first living child, along with conditional cash support for nutrition and health care during pregnancy and lactation. The benefit is transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank account through the Direct Benefit Transfer system.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Pregnant women and lactating mothers for the first living child
  • Women aged 19 years and above at the time of first pregnancy
  • Beneficiaries under PMMVY must follow the prescribed health and nutrition conditions
  • Excludes women covered under other maternity benefit schemes of the central government

Benefits

  • Cash benefit of Rs 5,000 in instalments during pregnancy and after delivery
  • Additional support under the maternity benefit programme of the state, where applicable
  • Encourages institutional delivery and proper nutrition during pregnancy
  • Direct transfer of the benefit to the beneficiary's bank account

How to Apply

  1. Register the pregnancy at the nearest Anganwadi centre or health facility
  2. Submit the application with the mother and child protection card
  3. Complete the health check-ups and immunisation schedule as required
  4. Receive the instalments in the bank account after verification

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card of the beneficiary and family
  • Bank account details with IFSC code
  • Mother and Child Protection Card
  • Pregnancy registration details
meta_title: PM Matru Vandana Yojana: Rs 5,000 Maternity Benefit
meta_description: PMMVY provides Rs 5,000 cash benefit in instalments for pregnant women and lactating mothers of the first child. Check eligibility and how to apply.

content:
Overview

One Stop Centres, also known as Sakhi Centres, are a scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development to support women affected by violence. The centres provide integrated support including police assistance, medical aid, legal aid, counselling, and temporary shelter under one roof. Women facing domestic violence, sexual abuse, or any form of violence can approach a Sakhi Centre in their district for free support services.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any woman facing physical, sexual, emotional, or economic violence can avail services
  • Women of all ages and backgrounds are eligible
  • Girls below 18 years are referred to child protection services as per procedure

Benefits

  • Immediate emergency response and temporary shelter
  • Medical examination and treatment facilitation
  • Police assistance and legal aid support
  • Psychological counselling and rehabilitation support

How to Apply

  1. Call the Women Helpline 181 or visit the nearest One Stop Centre directly
  2. Explain the situation to the centre staff
  3. Receive the required support services as per the individual case

Required Documents

  • No documents are required to approach the centre; services are provided on request
meta_title: One Stop Centre (Sakhi): Support for Women Facing Violence
meta_description: Sakhi One Stop Centres provide medical, legal, police, and counselling support to women facing violence. Learn how to access services.

content:
Overview

Women Helpline 181 is a 24-hour emergency helpline of the Ministry of Women and Child Development for women facing violence or distress. The helpline provides immediate counselling, referral, and support services for women in need across India. Calls can be made free of charge from any phone, and the helpline connects women to police, medical, legal, and shelter services as required.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any woman in distress or facing violence can call 181
  • The service is available 24 hours a day throughout the year
  • Family members and concerned citizens can also call for assistance

Benefits

  • Free 24-hour emergency assistance through a single number
  • Immediate counselling and crisis intervention
  • Referral to police, medical, legal, and shelter services
  • Follow-up support to ensure the woman receives the needed help

How to Apply

  1. Dial 181 from any phone, free of cost
  2. Describe the situation to the helpline counsellor
  3. Receive the necessary support and follow-up assistance

Required Documents

  • No documents are required to call the helpline
meta_title: Women Helpline 181: 24-Hour Support for Women in Distress
meta_description: Women Helpline 181 is a free 24-hour emergency helpline providing counselling and referral support to women facing violence or distress.

content:
Overview

Swadhar Greh is a scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development that provides shelter, food, clothing, and rehabilitation services to women in difficult circumstances. The scheme covers women who are victims of domestic violence, family conflict, or social ostracism, as well as women without any family support, such as widows, destitute women, and trafficked victims. Implementing agencies run the shelter homes with financial support from the government.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Women in difficult circumstances including victims of violence, trafficking, or abandonment
  • Women without family support such as widows and destitute women
  • Priority for women referred by the police, courts, or child protection system

Benefits

  • Safe shelter with food and clothing
  • Medical care and counselling services
  • Skill training and livelihood support for rehabilitation
  • Legal aid and support for reintegration with family or society

How to Apply

  1. Approach the nearest Swadhar Greh or the district women and child development office
  2. Complete the intake and assessment process
  3. Receive shelter and rehabilitation services as per the individual plan

Required Documents

  • Identity details as available; the shelter facilitates documentation where needed
meta_title: Swadhar Greh: Shelter & Rehabilitation for Women in Need
meta_description: Swadhar Greh provides shelter, food, medical care, and skill training to women in difficult circumstances. Check eligibility and how to seek help.

content:
Overview

The Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG), also known as Kishori Shakti Yojana, is a programme for out of school adolescent girls in the age group of 11 to 14 years. Implemented through Anganwadi centres, the scheme provides nutrition supplementation, iron and folic acid support, and life skills education. It aims to improve the nutritional and health status of adolescent girls and equip them with skills for better life outcomes.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Out of school adolescent girls aged 11 to 14 years
  • Priority for girls from disadvantaged and marginalised households
  • Girls enrolled through the Anganwadi network in implementing areas

Benefits

  • Supplementary nutrition through take home rations
  • Iron and folic acid supplementation to prevent anaemia
  • Life skills, health, and nutrition education sessions
  • Guidance on vocational training and social participation

How to Apply

  1. Enrol with the local Anganwadi worker in implementing areas
  2. Attend the weekly sessions at the Anganwadi centre
  3. Receive nutrition and health services as per the programme schedule

Required Documents

  • Age proof
  • Family identity details
meta_title: Scheme for Adolescent Girls: Nutrition & Life Skills Support
meta_description: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls provides nutrition, iron-folic acid, and life skills education to out-of-school girls aged 11-14. Check eligibility.

content:
Overview

The National Commission for Women (NCW) is a statutory body established in 1992 to safeguard the rights and interests of women in India. The commission reviews laws affecting women, investigates complaints of gender discrimination and violence, and recommends policy measures to the government. It also undertakes research, awareness, and advocacy on women's issues across the country.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Any woman can file a complaint with the commission regarding violation of her rights
  • Complaints related to domestic violence, dowry, sexual harassment, and discrimination are handled
  • The commission can also take suo motu action on issues reported in the media

Benefits

  • Complaint redressal for women facing discrimination or violence
  • Investigations and recommendations for action against offenders
  • Legal aid and support through the commission's network
  • Awareness programmes and research on women's rights

How to Apply

  1. File a complaint through the NCW online portal, email, or in person
  2. Provide details and evidence of the grievance
  3. The commission investigates and follows up with the concerned authorities

Required Documents

  • Complaint details with supporting evidence
  • Identity and contact details of the complainant
meta_title: National Commission for Women: Complaint & Support Services
meta_description: NCW safeguards women's rights, handling complaints of violence, discrimination, and harassment. Learn how to file a complaint with the commission.

content:
Overview

Mahila Shakti Kendras (MSK) are a scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development that works at the grassroots level for the empowerment of rural women. The Kendras provide a platform for women to access government schemes, skill development, and awareness programmes. They act as a convergence point connecting women with livelihood, health, legal, and digital literacy services at the district and block levels.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to all women in the implementing districts and blocks
  • Services are free at the Kendra level
  • Rural women, self help group members, and adolescent girls are the key target groups

Benefits

  • Information and facilitation for government schemes for women
  • Skill development and livelihood training programmes
  • Awareness sessions on health, nutrition, and legal rights
  • Support for self help groups and women's collectives

How to Apply

  1. Visit the Mahila Shakti Kendra in your district or block
  2. Register as a beneficiary with basic details
  3. Participate in the training and awareness programmes

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card
  • No other documents are generally required
meta_title: Mahila Shakti Kendra: Women Empowerment at Grassroots
meta_description: Mahila Shakti Kendras empower rural women with scheme access, skill training, and awareness programmes at district and block level. Learn more.

content:
Overview

The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, also known as the Women's Reservation Act 2023, is a landmark law that reserves one third of seats in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies, and the Delhi assembly for women. Passed in September 2023, the Act is a constitutional amendment that strengthens women's representation in legislatures. The reservation is to be implemented after the delimitation exercise and applies to all categories of seats including reserved constituencies.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Women candidates across all communities and categories are covered by the reservation
  • Seats are rotated among constituencies in a phased manner as per the Act
  • One third of the total seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies are reserved

Benefits

  • Guaranteed one third representation for women in central and state legislatures
  • Greater participation of women in law making and governance
  • Strengthens policies on women's welfare and development
  • Sets an example for inclusive political participation

How to Apply

  1. The reservation is implemented through the electoral process after the notified date
  2. Women candidates participate through the normal election process in reserved constituencies
  3. Eligible voters elect women representatives in the reserved seats

Required Documents

  • As per the electoral and candidate nomination process
meta_title: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam: 33% Women's Reservation Act
meta_description: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam 2023 reserves one third of Lok Sabha and state assembly seats for women. Understand the law and its implementation.

content:
Overview

The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) is a centrally sponsored scheme that provides a protective environment for children in difficult circumstances. The scheme supports institutional care through child care institutions, non-institutional care through foster care and adoption, and community based services through the child protection machinery. It funds the Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, and District Child Protection Units across states.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Children in need of care and protection, including orphans, abandoned, and abused children
  • Children in conflict with the law are covered through juvenile justice services
  • Families offering foster care or adoption can participate through the designated authorities

Benefits

  • Shelter, education, and rehabilitation for children in institutional care
  • Support for foster care, sponsorship, and adoption services
  • Emergency outreach through Childline and district child protection units
  • Training and capacity building of child protection functionaries

How to Apply

  1. Children in need can be brought to the Child Welfare Committee through Childline 1098
  2. Families can apply for foster care or sponsorship through the district child protection unit
  3. Adoption applications are processed through the Central Adoption Resource Authority

Required Documents

  • As specified by the Child Welfare Committee or the concerned authority
meta_title: Integrated Child Protection Scheme: Care for Children in Need
meta_description: ICPS provides institutional and non-institutional care, foster care, and adoption services for children in difficult circumstances. Learn more.
